SpamWise
Overview Support Privacy

Mail compatibility

SpamWise requires macOS 27 and Apple Mail. It has been tested on Apple-silicon Macs; Intel Macs and earlier macOS versions are untested and unsupported. Apple's on-device model also needs Apple Intelligence to be available and its model downloaded. SpamWise checks whether the provider you chose is available and never switches to another one by itself.

Accounts

SpamWise works with accounts you have added to Mail. It doesn't read Mail's databases and doesn't need Full Disk Access.

Account in Mail Status
iCloud Tested: Inbox and Junk moves, Review flag, corrections and Junk rescue
Google Tested: Inbox and Junk moves, Review flag
Exchange, Microsoft 365 and Outlook.com Not tested yet
Other accounts in Mail Not tested yet

Testing used generated messages on a few accounts; it isn't a guarantee for every account of that kind. Behavior while offline or reconnecting hasn't been tested yet.

Microsoft 365 and Outlook.com don't name their mail server in the Authentication-Results header they add. SpamWise instead takes the server's name from the ARC-Authentication-Results header Microsoft adds when the message arrives, shows it as a detected server with that explanation, and, once you trust it, trusts the results in Microsoft's own Authentication-Results header. Mail that reached you through a forwarder or mailing list that adds its own ARC headers gets no trusted results this way. You can also enter mx.microsoft.com yourself.

Mailboxes

SpamWise moves mail only to the Inbox and Junk mailboxes that Mail assigns to that account; it never picks a folder by its name. Check Mailboxes, under each account's Mailboxes and Details in Settings → Accounts, reads those assignments without opening any message or changing anything. If an account has no Junk mailbox, or more than one, SpamWise doesn't move that account's mail; the account's settings say how to fix it in Mail.

How moves are checked

After moving a message, SpamWise looks for it every two seconds and counts the move as done once it finds the message in its new mailbox twice in a row, giving up after 30 seconds. When those 30 seconds have passed it looks once more, and records the move as unconfirmed if the message is no longer the only copy there. This checks what Mail shows on the Mac; a mail server can still move the message later.

A message that you sent to yourself in the same account has a Sent copy with the same Message-ID, so SpamWise can't tell the two apart and leaves both alone. Automatic moves also leave mail without a Message-ID in place. Correcting such a message still moves it; SpamWise then finds it by its size and exact content to confirm the move.

If you move a message SpamWise put in Junk back to the Inbox, or choose Not Junk, SpamWise counts it as marked Good on its next check, once its own move has held for those 30 seconds. Learning from it doesn't move the message.

Other filters

SpamWise checks each account's Inbox through Mail about once a minute while SpamWise and Mail are both open and the Mac is awake. Mail also lists SpamWise's Mail extension, which leaves every message to Mail: Mail doesn't tell extensions which account a message belongs to, so all filtering happens through SpamWise's own checks.

Mail's built-in Junk Mail filter, SpamSieve and server rules keep working alongside SpamWise, and their moves and colors are separate from SpamWise's. Keep dry run on while you compare SpamWise with another filter; mail another filter moved to Junk is not treated as your own correction.

IMAP

Instead of Apple Mail, SpamWise can connect directly to one IMAP account (Settings → Accounts → Mail connection). That route hasn't been tested against a live server yet. It reads each message once, so mail it previews in dry run stays where it is when you start filtering. See IMAP.
